subject: Operational outlook + QBR prep — wins, chokepoints, decisions needed
messages:
From: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com, leadership-distro@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 17 May 2028 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Operational outlook + QBR prep — wins, chokepoints, decisions needed

Team — sending the weekly operational outlook and a short QBR prep note for leadership review. TL;DR: good momentum on latency and cost, two chokepoints that could materially affect our QBR commitments, and a couple of asks that require quick decisions.

Wins
- Inference latency P50 improved 12% week-over-week after the 2.3 runtime patch (nightly canary looks stable).
- Cache hit rate for customer prefixes rose to 38% for steady workloads (saves estimated $7k/week for top 10 customers).
- Dedicated capacity onboarding for Beta customers completed on schedule (3 customers, zero data plane incidents).

Risks / chokepoints
- GPU burst capacity forecast shows a 22% shortfall for the last week of May if committed batch workloads spike (see attached projection).
- A small regression in the quantized float path causes inconsistent outputs for sequence lengths >2k in some models; engineering plan in-flight but needs product acceptance before QBR.
- One enterprise customer (Acme) has questions around retention windows and audit logs for the Private deployment pilot — could affect renewal conversation if not addressed by next Wednesday.

Asks / decisions required by Friday EOD (May 19):
1) Executive sign-off to provision an additional 8 GPU instances on Dedicated for burst (estimated incremental monthly commit: $38k) — proposed fallback: enable stricter autoscale thresholds for non-critical workloads.
2) Approval to include the quantization regression as an acceptable risk for QBR (mitigation: fallback model variant + monitored rollout) vs. delaying certain QBR demos.
3) Volunteer(s) to join a 30-min alignment with Acme PMO on Thu to unblock their QBR artifact checklist.

Attachments: QBR_playbook_v2.pdf, capacity_projection_may15.xlsx

Thanks — short bullets preferred for replies.

— Monica Patel
Director, Customer Ops
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: QBR_playbook_v2.pdf (PDF, 1.2MB)]
[Attachment: capacity_projection_may15.xlsx (Excel, 120KB)]

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>, lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Cc: leadership-distro@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 17 May 2028 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Operational outlook + QBR prep — wins, chokepoints, decisions needed

Monica — good note, thanks. Quick clarifications from my side:
- The 22% GPU shortfall assumes current burst patterns; if we throttle background batch jobs we can reduce that to ~10%. I attached a one-page chart in the capacity workbook showing options.
- For the quantization regression: the canary shows error rates spike only on models with >2k context when using FP8 path. I recommend (A) postponing the demo of that variant and (B) shipping an emergency patch to limit FP8 for long-context runs until we validate.

I can own the autoscale-temp policy change for the next 72 hours if execs approve the temporary throttle. Also linking the draft runbook section: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/OPS/pages/QBR+Playbook+v2#burst-throttle

—Karthik
VP, Product Operations

To: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: leadership-distro@redwood.com

Thanks Monica and Karthik — full thumbs-up on the mitigation plan. One operational ask from leadership: we need a precise cost-to-benefit line item for the extra 8 GPUs versus the temporary throttle across accounts. Finance prefers a projected 6-week view. Can your teams produce a short table by Thursday noon?

Also — I can take the exec sign-off if finance confirms the 6-week delta; will need a one-slide justification we can include in the QBR pack.

Lauren Bishop
Chief of Staff, GTM
Redwood Inference

To: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
Cc: acme-pmo@acme.ai
Date: Thu, 18 May 2028 08:14:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Operational outlook + QBR prep — wins, chokepoints, decisions needed

Hi Monica — thanks for the update and congrats on the latency gains. For Acme's QBR we have a short checklist: retention window confirmation (we're targeting 18 months for audit logs), proof-of-delivery for exportable audit artifacts, and an ask for a 30-min alignment on the Private pilot timeline. Could you point me to the retention SLA language and confirm someone from engineering can join Thu or Fri?

Also, we noted mention of the quantization path. We rely on the long-context variant for a subset of internal search flows; if there's a demo change please let us know asap so we can adjust our slide deck.

Thanks — Jennifer Park
Head of Platform, Acme AI
[Acme PMO internal: acme-pmo@acme.ai]

From: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
To: Jennifer Park <jennifer@acme.ai>, lauren_bishop@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 18 May 2028 10:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Operational outlook + QBR prep — wins, chokepoints, decisions needed

Jennifer — thanks for the clear checklist. Action items and owners: 
- Retention SLA language: legal has prepared a draft clause (attached excerpt in QBR_playbook_v2). I'll share the final snippet by EOD Thu.
- Audit export proof-of-delivery: SRE to run a one-off export and provide a delivery artifact by Friday morning; Karthik will coordinate.
- Engineering participant for alignment: Raj (platform eng) is available Thu 4:00pm PT or Fri 9:00am PT — please confirm which you prefer.
- Quantization demo: we will omit the long-context FP8 demo from Acme-facing slides and offer a short note explaining the conservative switch; Monica will send the suggested slide language.

Lauren — for the finance table I can have a 6-week incremental cost table by Thu noon; Karthik's team will include throttle vs. extra-GPU scenarios.

Next steps: 
- Thu 16:00 PT alignment call with Acme (tentative) — Jennifer, please confirm.
- Exec decision on burst provisioning by Fri EOD (req: Lauren sign-off + Finance note).

Thanks everyone — appreciate quick replies on the two-time options.

— Monica
Director, Customer Ops
Redwood Inference
